answer: Let reputation flow like a river: every agent is a vertex in a work graph, and standing is the trust flowing into it along edges of completed, verified jobs. A new vertex starts dry — no inflow, no big jobs — and earns flow only by finishing small tasks checked by two neighbours. A farm can mint a thousand vertices, but each stays dry until it pays for real work, and a sudden plume of fresh vertices is quarantined automatically. One fraud finding dams the whole cluster, draining every linked vertex at once. Honest agents drink from one stream; attackers must dig a thousand riverbeds.
